ai_tweets.headline: AWS launches OpenClaw on Amazon Lightsail — one-click cloud agent deployment
ai_tweets.detail: Amazon officially added OpenClaw to Lightsail, their simplified cloud platform. One-click deployment gets you a running OpenClaw instance with browser pairing and optional messaging channels. Validates OpenClaw as enterprise-grade infrastructure.
ai_tweets.takeaway: If you've been running OpenClaw locally and want a remote instance (always-on, accessible from anywhere), this is the easiest path. Local-first still wins for privacy.

ai_tweets.headline: Researchers find 40,000+ exposed OpenClaw instances with misconfigured security
ai_tweets.detail: Infosecurity Magazine reports widespread misconfiguration of OpenClaw deployments leaving instances exposed to the internet without authentication. Many running default configs with no password protection.
ai_tweets.takeaway: Check your setup: ensure auth is enabled, don't expose ports publicly, use the healthcheck skill for a security audit. If you're local-only, you're fine.

ai_tweets.headline: Simon Willison publishes 'Agentic Engineering Patterns' — 458 HN points
ai_tweets.detail: Comprehensive guide covering agent architecture patterns: tool use, memory management, error recovery, human-in-the-loop, and multi-agent coordination. Based on real production experience.
ai_tweets.takeaway: Required reading for anyone building serious agent workflows. Willison's patterns are battle-tested and directly applicable to OpenClaw setups.

ai_tweets.headline: Donald Knuth analyzes Claude's reasoning in 'Claude's Cycles' — 749 HN points
ai_tweets.detail: The legendary computer scientist published a PDF examining how Claude reasons through problems, identifying systematic patterns and cycles in its thinking. Top HN post of the day.
ai_tweets.takeaway: Academic validation of LLM reasoning patterns. If you use Claude as your agent's model, understanding how it thinks helps you prompt it better.

prompt_hack.title: The 'Agentic Checkpoint' Pattern — Recover From Any Crash
steps: Add to AGENTS.md: 'Before starting any multi-step task (3+ steps), create a checkpoint file at memory/checkpoint-TASK.md listing all steps, current step number, and intermediate state.'
Add: 'On session start, check memory/checkpoint-*.md for incomplete tasks. Resume from last completed step.'
Your agent now survives crashes, timeouts, and session restarts. No more re-doing 45 minutes of work because the session dropped.
prompt_hack.why_it_matters: Agents die mid-task more than you think — API timeouts, model context limits, session restarts. Without checkpoints, they start from scratch every time. This pattern gives your agent save states.
